questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT one of the four components of an index?
questions.explanation: The four components of a typical index are headings (main entries), subheadings (subentries), locators, and cross-references (See and See also). An abstract summarises a document and is not a component of an index.

questions.stem: Which statement correctly distinguishes a table of contents from an index?

options.A: A table of contents appears at the beginning and follows the order of the book, while an index usually appears at the end and is arranged alphabetically.
options.B: A table of contents is arranged alphabetically, while an index follows the order of the book.
options.C: A table of contents gives detailed access to specific topics, while an index only lists chapter titles.
options.D: There is no real difference; the two serve exactly the same purpose.

questions.explanation: The table of contents appears at the beginning of a book and follows the order of the book, showing its structure. The index usually appears at the end, is arranged alphabetically, and provides detailed access to specific information.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT listed as a type of book index?
questions.explanation: The chapter lists subject, author, name, title, geographical, chronological, citation, analytical, keyword and combined indexes. An annotated index is not among the major types described.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT one of the ten stages typically involved in preparing a book index?
questions.explanation: The ten stages run from reading the book and subject analysis through to editing and proofreading. Peer review is not one of the stages listed in the chapter.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a challenge commonly faced by book indexers?

options.A: Deciding whether the index should appear at the beginning or at the end of the book.
options.B: Selecting appropriate terminology and managing interdisciplinary topics, synonyms and homonyms.
options.C: Keeping the chapters of the book in alphabetical order.
options.D: Avoiding the use of See and See also references.

questions.explanation: Book indexing is time-consuming, demands consistency, and requires indexers to select appropriate terminology, deal with interdisciplinary topics, and manage synonyms and homonyms. Page shifts and tight deadlines add to the pressure.
